transcript:
Header: 
Date: 2026-12-02
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Daniel Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Orion CTO), Liam O'Connor (Orion Head of ML), Sara Kim (Orion DevOps)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Daniel our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:05] Priya: Good, thanks. Busy week but excited to dig in.
[00:12] Daniel: Awesome. Quick agenda — model selection, context length needs, multilingual requirements, tool-calling and infra options (hosted/dedicated/private), and then next steps. Anything to add?
[00:20] Liam: Nope that's perfect. We'll jump right in with our use case.
[00:30] Priya: So high level — Orion is building a customer support + knowledge retrieval layer over our docs and call transcripts. We need a model that can handle long contexts — we're looking at up to 100k tokens for some retrieval-augmented flows, and multi-lingual support (EN, FR, DE, JA). Latency important but cost is also a concern at scale.
[00:50] Maya: Got it. When you say 100k, is that active KV cache usage or full prompt length including tool inputs?
[00:58] Liam: Mostly retrieval context — we chunk docs and want the model to ingest large retrieved context. We also call APIs/tools for enrichment (calendar lookups, internal DB queries). Tool-calling is non-negotiable for us.
[01:10] Daniel: Okay, so two big requirements: long context handling and tool-calling. For long contexts we typically recommend model families that support extended context — we can also use KV caching and prefix caching at the runtime level. Note, some open models advertise 100k but performance varies.
[01:28] Priya: Can you walk through hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs here? For compliance, we may need VPC or on-prem eventually.
[01:36] Maya: Sure — hosted is fastest to deploy and lowest operational overhead, good for prototyping. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity, consistent latency and data isolation (but still in our infra). Private is customer-managed control plane or on-prem for strict compliance. For 100k tokens, Dedicated or Private tend to be better for stable latency because you can pin heavier GPU types and tune batching.
[01:56] Sara: What about encryption and keys? We have KMS and HSM requirements.
[02:00] Daniel: We integrate with customer KMS, support BYO keys for Private; Dedicated also supports KMS integrations and audit logs. We'll send the SOC2 and ISO pack after.
[02:09] Priya: Competitors — we've looked at OpenAI for hosted, and some vendors like Anthropic and Cohere for model quality. We're also evaluating self-hosted options to control cost.
[02:20] Maya: Makes sense. For open models, do you have any preference? Llama-style, Mistral, MPT, or the newer long-context variants?
[02:30] Liam: We prefer open models, yes. Cost and fine-tuning flexibility important. We also need deterministic tool-calling behavior — ability to do structured outputs and function calling reliably.
[02:42] Daniel: On function calling, Redwood has first-class support for tool calls and structured outputs. Small note — some transcribers call it function- uh, function-calling. The runtime will ensure we stream tool call requests and manage the handoff.
[02:55] Priya: Are there known open models that support 100k natively?
[02:58] Daniel: There are experimental models — some community forks and research versions of Llama and others using sliding-window and sparse attention. Practically, we often pair a long-context model for embedding/recall plus chunked prompts with KV cache; or use retrieval-first architectures where you only pass the top k chunks.
[03:18] Liam: So does Redwood do automatic retrieval augmentation?
[03:21] Maya: We provide tooling recommendations — Redwood Optimize suggests batching and caching policies; for retrieval we can integrate vector DBs and provide sample pipelines. We don't host your vector DB by default but can connect to Pinecone/FAISS/Chroma.
[03:35] Sara: Latency numbers? If we target 1-2s for generation on 8k tokens that's fine; but with 100k retrieval we expect increased latency.
[03:42] Daniel: Latency will scale with context. On Dedicated with optimized kernels and quantized models, you can get better throughput. For 100k context — often you won't send the entire 100k as a single prompt; you'd retrieve top chunks and use KV cache to reduce repeated prefixes. We can run benchmarks with your prompts to measure tail latency.
[03:58] Priya: Multilingual quality — we've got a lot of French and Japanese content. Do open models handle that well?
[04:05] Liam: Some do, some don't. Mistral and Llama-2 variants mixed. There are also multi-lingual models like XLM variants, but they may lag in instruction-following. We'd want to test.
[04:15] Daniel: Exactly — we'll run a multilingual eval during the POC. We'll need sample prompts and evaluation metrics from you (BLEU isn't great for instruction tasks; we'll use task-specific F1/ROUGE plus human review).
[04:29] Priya: About cost — do you have per-token pricing for hosted vs dedicated?
[04:33] Maya: Hosted pricing is usage-based. Dedicated is reserved capacity with a monthly commit, usually more cost-effective at scale. We'll send a detailed pricing sheet.
[04:40] Liam: Any caveats about fine-tuning vs LoRA?
[04:43] Daniel: On Dedicated and Private you can do LoRA and parameter-efficient tuning; hosted may have restrictions depending on model licensing. For open models, LoRA is common.
[04:50] Priya: Security questions — SSO, RBAC, audit logs?
[04:53] Maya: We support SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, request-level logging in Dedicated/Private with configurable retention. We'll share the security pack.
[05:02] Sara: Network setup for Private — is it fully air-gapped possible?
[05:06] Daniel: Yes for on-prem private deployments we have packages that run without contacting Redwood control plane if desired. For VPC, you get customer-managed networking. We'll coordinate with your infra team for the network diagram.
[05:18] Priya: Great. On the model front — we'd like Redwood to recommend a shortlist of open models to try: a performant LLM with 32k context, an experimental long-context 100k candidate, and a strong multilingual 8k/32k.
[05:32] Maya: We'll do that. Tentative shortlist: 1) Mistral-Chat-32k variant (or similar) for balanced latency/quality; 2) a 100k long-context community model (we'll denote as 'Long-Context-X' in the deliverables); 3) Llama-2 70B quantized for instruction and fine-tuning; and 4) a multilingual model like BLOOMZ or a fine-tuned Llama variant for FR/JA. We'll include pros/cons per your workload.
[05:56] Liam: For the experimental 100k one, do you recommend Dedicated or Private?
[05:59] Daniel: Dedicated for controlled latency and easier ops; Private if you need full control and KMS/HSM on-prem. Dedicated is usually the sweet spot to start.
[06:07] Priya: Fine. Let's discuss timeline and success criteria. Our timeline is end of Q1 to have a pilot running in production. Success criteria: 1) Avg latency under X ms for normal flows (we'll define X), 2) F1 > baseline on QA tasks, 3) security sign-off.
[06:23] Maya: Sounds good. We'll propose a pilot plan: 6 weeks POC with data-handling plan, benchmarks, and a small dedicated pool if needed.
[06:31] Priya: What do you need from us?
[06:33] Daniel: Sample prompt sets, representative documents for retrieval, target languages and volumes, and a list of tool APIs you need us to integrate with. Also any compliance requirements (e.g., SOC2 controls, data residency).
[06:47] Priya: We'll share those — action items on our side.
[06:50] Maya: Great. Any other questions?
[06:53] Sara: One small one — you mentioned automatic caching, does that handle session-level personalization?
[06:58] Daniel: Yes, KV cache can be per-session; we also have prefix caching to keep commonly used system prompts cached. For privacy we can configure retention policies.
[07:10] Liam: Love it. Let's recap next steps.
[07:12] Maya: Recap — Maya will send pricing and security docs; Daniel will prepare benchmark plan and shortlist of models; Orion will send prompt sets and infra constraints; schedule SE deep dive next week to run a mini benchmark.
[07:28] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:32] Maya: Thank you, talk soon.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts (e.g., "K V cash" instead of KV cache, "V P C" for VPC). References to deliverables: pricing-sheet.pdf (shared), security-pack.zip (to be shared), sample-benchmarks.xlsx (to be created).
